issues.description: `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` raises a warning class as an exception - wrong shape entirely
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a warning, not an error. Raising it as an exception is broken semantics: either warn via warnings.warn() and proceed, or raise a real exception like ValueError. The test uses pytest.raises on a warning class, which masks the confusion. Pick one: warn-and-continue or refuse-with-error. Don't do both badly.

issues.description: Dead `break` after `raise` - unreachable code that signals the author didn't read their own diff
issues.detail: Line after `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is `break`. The raise unwinds the loop; break never executes. This is the kind of thing that gets caught by reading the diff once before submitting. Remove it. If the intent was to warn-and-break, then the raise is wrong. Either way the code is wrong.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` computation uses product over all axes - wrong unit for a per-axis check
issues.detail: The loop checks per-axis misalignment but the suggested remedy multiplies `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * itemsize`. For multi-dim arrays this overshoots: a user told to set chunk-size to the full shard volume when only one axis was misaligned will get larger chunks than necessary. Also `max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` is suspicious - when is itemsize ever zero?

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` is unreadable - operator precedence trap
issues.detail: Python parses this as `not (nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0)`, which is what's intended, but `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:` says the same thing in one less mental hop. The current form is the kind of thing a maintainer reads twice. Don't make them.

issues.description: Only checks `dw[0]` - assumes uniform chunks but auto_chunks can return non-uniform tails
issues.detail: `normalize_chunks` returns tuples where the last chunk is often smaller. The check inspects only the nominal first chunk and ignores the tail. For shard alignment this is usually fine because the tail is the remainder, but the code should either justify why dw[0] suffices in a comment or check all chunks. Right now it's an implicit assumption with no test.

issues.description: Open question in the PR description shipped as committed code - decide before merging
issues.detail: The PR author asks: should this be an exception or a config-change prompt? That question is unresolved and the code answers it by raising a warning-as-exception. Resolve the design question, then ship the patch that matches the resolution. Don't merge a patch whose author is still asking what shape it should be.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The core idea - use shard shape as previous_chunks so auto_chunks lands on a shard-aligned multiple - is good taste. The execution has two bugs that should not survive a self-review: a warning class raised as an exception, and an unreachable `break` after `raise`. The `safe_chunk_size` calculation uses np.prod across all axes for what is a per-axis check, which gives users wrong remediation advice on multi-dim arrays. The PR description itself contains an unresolved design question (warn vs raise) - resolve that, fix the dead code, then resubmit.
